color.note: Midnight is the brand's native state and the first theme (AGF // FIELD: deepest-forest chassis). Daylight is the paper theme for manuals, packaging interiors, certificates and bright web sections. Air is the OLED/broadcast calibration (AGF // AIR: obsidian faceplates, true-black displays). surface-deep is the deepest forest in every theme.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: The page ground. Midnight: deepest forest. Daylight: bone paper. Air: obsidian, true black on OLED.

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Sections, cards and panels one step above surface. The forest floor.

tokens.name: surface-lifted
tokens.usage: Hovered or active cards, chips, the top of a stack. In Midnight only ink and brass-glow are legible on it; keep ink-muted and brass-text off it.

tokens.name: surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Pressed states, input wells, table stripes, the meter trough. Air: the recessed cage behind a rack module.

tokens.name: surface-deep
tokens.usage: Always dark in both themes: footers, hero scrims, packaging sleeves, hardware faceplates. Text on it is ink-on-deep or ink-on-deep-muted.

tokens.name: scrim
tokens.usage: Over photography behind text, and beneath dialogs.

tokens.name: glass
tokens.usage: Glass panels floating over imagery or a trace field, paired with blur-glass and a brass-hairline border.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Headlines and body copy on every surface token in both themes (6.2:1 or better).

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Ledes, secondary copy, quotes, dark-section prose. Midnight: on surface, surface-raised and surface-sunken, not surface-lifted (3.8:1 there, large text only).

tokens.name: ink-faint
tokens.usage: Captions, eyebrows, sources, table headers at 12-13px. Legible on surface, surface-raised and surface-sunken in both themes.

tokens.name: ink-on-deep
tokens.usage: Headlines and body on surface-deep.

tokens.name: ink-on-deep-muted
tokens.usage: Secondary copy on surface-deep. The pale stone of the dark section.

tokens.name: obsidian
tokens.usage: The deepest contrast. Daylight's ink, and the text colour on any brass or signal fill in both themes.

tokens.name: forest
tokens.usage: The brand green as a solid: Daylight headlines and rules, packaging fields, swatch references. In Midnight it is a surface, never an ink.

tokens.name: moss
tokens.usage: Decorative only: disabled text, dial tick marks, placeholder rules. Below 4.5:1 on every ground, so never body or captions.

tokens.name: brass
tokens.usage: The brand brass as a fill: the mark on dark grounds, primary buttons, bold rules, meter needles. Midnight: also text 24px+ on surface and surface-sunken. Daylight: fills only; words use brass-text.

tokens.name: brass-text
tokens.usage: Links, accent words, active nav items, numeric accents. On surface, surface-raised and surface-sunken in both themes.

tokens.name: brass-glow
tokens.usage: Link hover, the light-on-dark glow, the lit segment of a dial. Midnight: the one brass legible on surface-lifted.

tokens.name: brass-specular
tokens.usage: 24K specular: a 1px highlight on a knob rim or chamfer, the peak-hold dot on a meter, the OLED frequency curve. Never a fill or text; in Daylight it falls back to the dark brass so the highlight still reads.

tokens.name: on-brass
tokens.usage: Text and icons on a brass fill: the primary button label, a seal pressed into brass.

tokens.name: brass-hairline
tokens.usage: Hairline dividers, card borders, PCB traces, table rules. Decorative; a border that carries meaning uses line-strong.

tokens.name: line-strong
tokens.usage: Borders that mean something: inputs, selected cards, the active tab. At least 3:1 on surface, surface-raised and surface-sunken.

tokens.name: focus-ring
tokens.usage: Keyboard focus: a 2px gap in the ground colour, then a solid 2px ring. 4.5:1 or better on every surface token.

tokens.name: signal-nominal
tokens.usage: Meter segments below -12 dBFS, online, lock and sync states, the vectorscope phosphor trail. Always beside a scale or a word, never the only signal.

tokens.name: signal-hot
tokens.usage: Meter segments from -12 to -3 dBFS, warnings, 'hot' labels.

tokens.name: signal-clip
tokens.usage: Clip at 0 dBFS, error, mute engaged, ON AIR tally. A mark or a fill (3.3:1 or better on every surface); as a fill it carries on-signal text. Differs from signal-nominal by 3:1 in lightness in every theme.

tokens.name: on-signal
tokens.usage: Text on a signal-clip or signal-nominal fill (the ON AIR badge label).

tokens.name: live
tokens.usage: Alias of signal-clip for broadcast UI: the ON AIR lamp and tally.

styles.name: mark-mega
styles.usage: The hero mark. Brass on surface-deep. Only the letters A G F, never a word.

styles.name: mark
styles.usage: Nav, packaging, faceplates. The default size of the mark.

styles.name: mark-small
styles.usage: Footers, badges, the smallest the mark goes on screen; the stacked lines close up below 20px. In print, 8 mm cap height minimum.

styles.name: strapline-hero
styles.usage: One line of the most important words on a page, uppercase, tracked wide. A hero, a box lid, a dedication.

styles.name: strapline
styles.usage: Beneath the mark in the lockup; a product family name on a faceplate.

styles.name: strapline-small
styles.usage: A whispered caption under a section title. Uppercase only; the hairline strokes vanish in lowercase at this size.

styles.name: mega
styles.usage: Hero statements and the 'wow' tier. Thin weight so the brass mark beside it stays the heaviest thing on the page.

styles.name: display
styles.sample: Nothing between you and the signal
styles.usage: Section headlines (H1/H2). Editorial and print may set font-variation-settings "FLAR" 30 to flare the terminals toward Poiret One; UI never does.

styles.name: h3
styles.usage: Subheads, card titles in a feature grid. "FLAR" 30 allowed in editorial, as for display.

styles.name: lede
styles.sample: A preamp that disappears, so the room does not.
styles.usage: The first paragraph after a headline, pull quotes. Set in ink-muted.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Transformer-balanced outputs, galvanically isolated from chassis ground.

styles.name: body-strong
styles.sample: Phantom power: 48 V, 10 mA per channel.
styles.usage: Emphasis inside body, button labels, table row labels.

styles.name: small
styles.sample: Measured at 1 kHz, 150 Ω source, 20 Hz-20 kHz unweighted.
styles.usage: Dense UI, footnotes, legal, spec table cells.

styles.name: eyebrow
styles.usage: Uppercase label above a headline or a card, in ink-faint or brass-text. The Commissioner cousin of the strapline; use this for anything that is not one of the most important things.

styles.name: micro
styles.usage: Hardware panel legends and screen-printed labels. Uppercase, brass on surface-deep, 2 mm cap height minimum in print.

groups.name: Data — Commissioner

styles.name: data-mega
styles.usage: Hero numbers in a data callout. Tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums); the unit sits beside it in data-small.

styles.name: data
styles.usage: Readouts, key specs, gauge values. Tabular figures.

styles.name: data-small
styles.usage: Units beside a data number, secondary readouts, meter peak-hold values.

groups.note: Data styles lock "FLAR" 0, "VOLM" 0 and tabular figures so meters, prices and spec columns align.

spacing.note: An 8px grid with one 4px micro-step. 4-8 for icon-to-label gaps, 16-32 inside components, 48-64 between elements in a section, 80-120 between sections.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Micro gap: icon to label, badge padding.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Inline gaps, button icon gap, meter segment pitch.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: Component padding, list item gaps.

tokens.name: space-24
tokens.usage: Card padding, input height rhythm.

tokens.name: space-32
tokens.usage: Panel padding, gutter between cards.

tokens.name: space-48
tokens.usage: Between elements inside a section.

tokens.name: space-64
tokens.usage: Between a headline block and its content.

tokens.name: space-80
tokens.usage: Between sections on narrow screens.

tokens.name: space-96
tokens.usage: Between sections on wide screens.

tokens.name: space-120
tokens.usage: Hero padding, the breath before a footer.

radius.note: Barely there. Engineering hardware has chamfers, not bubbles.

tokens.name: radius-2
tokens.usage: Inputs, table cells, meter segments, hardware labels.

tokens.name: radius-4
tokens.usage: Buttons, badges with square ends, small cards.

tokens.name: radius-8
tokens.usage: Cards, panels, glass surfaces, dialogs.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: Status badges only (ON AIR, REC, 48 kHz). Never buttons.

tokens.name: border-hairline
tokens.usage: Dividers, card borders, PCB traces, table rules, in brass-hairline.

tokens.name: border-rule
tokens.usage: Section rules, the active nav underline, the focus ring, in brass or focus-ring.

tokens.name: border-bold
tokens.usage: A section opener, a quote bar, the meter zero line, in brass.

shadow.note: Depth comes from surface steps and hairlines; shadows are rare and soft, and the one glow is brass.

tokens.name: shadow-panel
tokens.usage: Glass panels and dialogs floating over imagery. Not for cards on a flat surface.

tokens.name: shadow-glow
tokens.usage: The soft brass halo behind a lit lamp, a hovered primary button, or the peak segment of a meter.

tokens.name: blur-glass
tokens.usage: backdrop-filter for glass panels. Pair with the glass colour token.

tokens.name: opacity-grain
tokens.usage: Film grain overlay on hero imagery (the agf-grain pattern). 0.04 over faces, 0.08 over flat colour.

tokens.name: opacity-trace
tokens.usage: The PCB trace field at rest. Up to 0.5 where a trace is the subject, as behind a data callout.

tokens.name: opacity-disabled
tokens.usage: Disabled controls and their labels.

tracking.note: Letter-spacing lives on the type styles; these three are exposed for consumers composing their own.

tokens.name: tracking-strapline
tokens.usage: Poiret One uppercase at hero size.

tokens.name: tracking-eyebrow
tokens.usage: Commissioner uppercase eyebrows and micro labels.

tokens.name: tracking-mark
tokens.usage: Between the letters of the Monoton mark.
